clue.text: Flippant delegate finally throttled by dissident

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word it follows, nothing more
something throttled is gripped round the neck, so the letter sits squeezed inside the other word

blocks.note: a factious person stirs up dissent within a group
the last letter of delegate

explanation.surface: A delegate gets silenced, perhaps literally strangled, by a rebel within the party.
explanation.walkthrough: FACTIOUS holds the E after its C to give FACETIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious remarks treat serious matters with inappropriate humour, which is what flippant means.

clue.text: Much primarily adrift in edges of foam?

definitions.text: Much primarily adrift in edges of foam?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word counts
the edges of a word are its two outermost letters
one thing set in another means its letters are placed between the outer ones

blocks.note: lots means much, a great deal
the opening letter of adrift
the first and last letters of foam

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a lot of stuff is drifting about at the edge of the surf.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: flotsam is largely debris floating in the foam at the shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is wreckage and debris found floating on the sea, much of it adrift among the surf.

clue.text: Ignore what hackers do

blocks.note: first meaning: to snub someone deliberately
second meaning: hackers hack, that is chop or slash

explanation.walkthrough: Hackers suggests computer intruders; here they are people chopping with blades.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone dead is to snub them, and to hack is to cut roughly with an axe or knife.

clue.text: Small drainage channel fly got out of, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound of the words matters

blocks.note: to tear is to fly along at speed, and to duck something is to get out of it

explanation.surface: A tiny ditch that some insect managed to escape from, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly looks like the insect, and drainage like plumbing; both belong to the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The tear duct is the narrow canal draining tears from the eye into the nose, a tiny drainage channel.

clue.text: Characters from panto freely available

indicators.note: taking only the characters from a word frees them to be placed in any order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Actors from a pantomime are easily available for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: Panto, short for pantomime, is a British Christmas stage show for families; its characters are here just its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer on tap flows straight from the barrel, so the idiom means available whenever wanted.

clue.text: Nurse as a rule going topless in seductive fashion

indicators.note: losing the top removes the first letter of the word

blocks.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, an old British nursing grade
usually means as a rule

explanation.surface: A nurse who habitually goes topless in an alluring way.
explanation.walkthrough: Topless paints a racy picture, but it just strips the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensually means in a way appealing to the physical senses, which is to say seductively.

clue.text: Maestro in Palladium set the tempo

indicators.note: one item placed in another means its letters go inside that other item's letters

blocks.note: Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium
an ace is an expert, a maestro

explanation.surface: A conductor at the London Palladium theatre sets the pace for the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Palladium is a famous theatre, but here palladium is the metal, Pd.
explanation.definitionFit: To pace a performance is to set how quickly it moves, its speed or tempo.

clue.text: Long-winded expert just short of sixty

blocks.note: a pro, a professional, is an expert
LIX is 59 in Roman numerals, one short of sixty

explanation.surface: A tedious specialist who is nearly sixty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolix speech or writing uses too many words, so it is wordy and tediously long.

clue.text: Restrain man who cures addict with consuming passion

blocks.note: to chain is to restrain
someone who cures fish or meat by smoking it

explanation.surface: Holding back a doctor who treats an addict, and a passionate one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: Cures suggests medicine, but it is the curing of food with smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain-smoker lights one cigarette from the last, an addict whose passion is literally burned up.

clue.text: Most learned to loathe record for the first time

indicators.note: read as in place of the first T, so that letter is swapped out

blocks.note: to detest is to loathe
an EP, extended play, is a kind of record

explanation.surface: The wisest person comes to hate a record on first hearing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the first time' reads as on first occasion, but splits as for the first T: the record replaces the first T of DETEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep thinker is profound and erudite, so the deepest is the most learned.

clue.text: Public appearance in Coventry?

definitions.note: a state, while the answer is a person in that state

blocks.note: out in the open, made public
a cast of face or features is one's appearance

explanation.surface: Someone making a public appearance in the city of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for ostracising them, refusing to speak to them; the question mark flags the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected by society, exactly the one who has been sent to Coventry.

clue.text: Baby son's left behind when one criminal goes inside

indicators.note: the son has gone away, so the letter abbreviating son drops out
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
going inside places these letters within the other word, as a convict goes inside a prison

blocks.note: nates is the anatomical word for the buttocks
s is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baby boy is abandoned when his father, a criminal, is sent to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind looks like an adverb meaning left over; here it is a noun, the buttocks, and nates is the Latin anatomical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, the medical term for a baby in its first weeks.

clue.text: Well-drilled players foul — one left back sent off

indicators.note: back says these two letters run in the opposite direction
a footballer sent off leaves the pitch, so these letters leave the word

blocks.note: squalid means filthy, foul
the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A disciplined team commits a foul, and a left back is shown the red card.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is football: a left back is a defender. Here the letters for one and left are reversed and removed from SQUALID, leaving SQUAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a group of players, and drill evokes the military squad trained to act together.

clue.text: Up to seven guards with light?

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it, so these letters enclose the next

blocks.note: anything up to seven is under eight
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Seven guards at most, armed with a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that light means not heavy rather than a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Underweight means weighing less than normal, so too light.

clue.text: Voyeur's characteristic version of epic re-run

indicators.note: a new version of something presents the same material in a different form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A peeping Tom's defining trait, perhaps from rewatching an epic on repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurience is an excessive interest in sexual matters, the trait that drives a voyeur to watch.

clue.text: Reformed male restricts gamblin', with beneficial effect

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, while the answer is the adjective describing such an effect

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
to restrict is to hem in, so these letters close around the others

blocks.note: taken as written
gambling is dicing, and the apostrophe drops its final G

explanation.surface: A man who gave up gambling found the change did him good.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G of gamblin’ is the hint that the gambling word also loses its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal describes something that heals or does good, such as a drink taken for its curative properties.

clue.text: Recollected losing cat down Memory Lane

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered together again, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a pet cat they lost long ago, wandering down Memory Lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Recollected looks like remembered, a definition; read as collected again, it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip down Memory Lane is a sentimental look back at the past, which is what nostalgic means.

clue.text: Fail to recall old Greek character — name forgotten

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so that letter is dropped
recall read as call back: the letters are brought back the way they came

blocks.note: Timon of Athens, the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone cannot remember an ancient Greek figure, the name having slipped their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail to recall' reads as one phrase meaning forget; split it so that Fail is the definition and to recall turns TIMO round.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit to do something is to fail to do it, as in he omitted to mention it.

clue.text: Soft fabric suit worn by Queen twice ...

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone goes around them, so these letters wrap the others

blocks.note: a suit at law is a case
two ways of writing the Queen: HM, Her Majesty, and ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen twice wearing a suit of soft material.
explanation.walkthrough: Suit looks like clothing, which fits the fabric surface, but it is a lawsuit; HM and ER go inside CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, woven into luxurious cloth.

clue.text: Painful affliction often seen in ears

blocks.note: first meaning: a painful patch of hard skin on the foot
second meaning: a cereal crop, which grows in ears

explanation.surface: A painful complaint that commonly turns up in people's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Ears suggests the organs of hearing, but here they are the seed heads of a cereal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn is a sore thickening of skin, and a cereal crop such as wheat or maize grows its grain in ears.

clue.text: Queen's visit getting hostile reception

blocks.note: a queen is a female cat
to call on someone is to visit

explanation.surface: The Queen pays a visit and is jeered by the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is the word for a female cat; the 's joins it to the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a shrill whistle or jeer of disapproval, the sound of a hostile audience.

clue.text: One illegally flying the flag in island meets resistance

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means its letters go inside that other word

blocks.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides
a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow, as in Union Jack
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A pirate flies an illegal flag on an island and is met with resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying the flag' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyjacker seizes control of an aircraft in flight, a criminal who is flying unlawfully.

clue.text: Low joint in road caused constant annoyance

indicators.note: one thing set in another means its letters go between the other's letters

blocks.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road
the ankle is the joint lowest on the body

explanation.surface: A dive bar on the high street that was a perpetual nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: A low joint sounds like a seedy bar, but it is a part of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles keeps causing bitterness or irritation long after the event.

clue.text: Confidence finally lost touring unknown country

indicators.note: with the end lost, the word's last letter is dropped
a tour goes round a place, so these letters encircle the next

blocks.note: belief means confidence, trust
an unknown quantity in algebra, like x and y

explanation.surface: A traveller loses their nerve while touring an unfamiliar land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confidence finally lost' could mean its last letter E goes; it is the whole of BELIEF that loses its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Belize is a nation in Central America, on the Caribbean coast south of Mexico.

clue.text: Children's favourite uncle's last to leave, after the others

indicators.note: last points at the final letter of the word it is attached to

blocks.note: them, those other people
the final letter of uncle
to park a car is to leave it somewhere

explanation.surface: The children's best-loved uncle is always the last to go home after everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: After says the uncle's letter and the leave word come behind the others word.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme park, with its rides and attractions, is a typical favourite outing for young children.

clue.text: Triumphed in Nick's case — over and out

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so only the word's outer letters are kept
one thing placed in another means its letters sit inside
turned over, the whole thing is read the other way round

blocks.note: the outer letters of Nick
won means triumphed

explanation.surface: A detective named Nick solves the case, then signs off as if on a radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over and out' is radio sign-off talk, but over turns the letters round and out is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When a secret is out, it is known publicly.

clue.text: Big bird partially responsible for another one

indicators.note: partially says only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters within them

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A large bird is partly to blame for the existence of another one, as a parent is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of another and the start of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a tall wading bird, one of the largest birds commonly seen by rivers in Britain.

clue.text: Shooter briefly stops a band in contention

indicators.note: something put briefly is cut short, so its final letter goes
a stopper plugs the middle of something, so these letters go inside the others

blocks.note: a gun is a shooter
taken as written
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A gunman halts a band's performance at a disputed event.
explanation.walkthrough: Band suggests musicians in this surface, but it is a ring such as one worn on a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people arguing are in contention, that is in dispute with each other.

clue.text: Cooker, not new, slowing down on the whole

indicators.note: not tells us that what follows is absent, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: an oven is a cooker
N is the abbreviation for new
rall. is the musical abbreviation of rallentando, meaning gradually slowing

explanation.surface: An old cooker that is gradually slowing down in general.
explanation.walkthrough: RALL. abbreviates the Italian rallentando, a direction to a musician to slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall and on the whole both mean taking everything into account, in general.

clue.text: Regularly employed in carpet-fitting

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of carpet

explanation.surface: Someone works steadily as a carpet fitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet-fitting looks like one trade; the hyphen hides the split between carpet and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or appropriate, which is what fitting means as an adjective.

clue.text: Turner's "Bubbles"? Not right!

definitions.note: possessive: read as a turner's tool

indicators.note: not right says the letter for right is taken away

blocks.note: lather is a mass of soap bubbles
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether Bubbles is by the painter Turner and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubbles is Millais's famous painting, not Turner's; but the turner here is a woodworker, and his tool is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A turner shapes wood or metal on a lathe, so the lathe is the turner's machine.

clue.text: Arrogant Tory not standing, they say

indicators.note: they say points to how words are spoken rather than how they are written

blocks.note: a Tory is a Con, short for Conservative, and not standing is seated

explanation.surface: A haughty Conservative politician who is not standing for election.
explanation.walkthrough: Not standing suggests not running for office, but it is simply sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person has an inflated opinion of themselves, the same vanity as an arrogant one.
